### Step 6: Installing and Reloading a Skill

Once the skill is packaged into a `.skill` file, offer to install it for the user. Ask whether they would like to install it locally in the current folder (workspace scope) or at the user level (user scope).

If the user agrees to an installation, perform it immediately using the `run_shell_command` tool:

- **Locally (workspace scope)**:
  ```bash
  gemini skills install <path/to/skill-name.skill> --scope workspace
  ```
- **User level (user scope)**:
  ```bash
  gemini skills install <path/to/skill-name.skill> --scope user
  ```

**Important:** After the installation is complete, notify the user that they MUST manually execute the `/skills reload` command in their interactive Gemini CLI session to enable the new skill. They can then verify the installation by running `/skills list`.

Note: You (the agent) cannot execute the `/skills reload` command yourself; it must be done by the user in an interactive instance of Gemini CLI. Do not attempt to run it on their behalf.

arguments.content:
---
name: slack-api
description: Interact with the Slack Web API to post and schedule messages, reply in threads, list channels, read channel history, create channels, upload files, and look up users. Use when the user asks to send or read Slack messages, manage Slack channels, upload files to Slack, or otherwise work with a Slack workspace programmatically.
---

# Slack API

Interact with a Slack workspace through the Slack Web API using the bundled Node.js scripts. All scripts need Node.js 18+ and a `SLACK_TOKEN` environment variable; they print clear success or error output and never dump stack traces.

## Setup

1. Export the token: `export SLACK_TOKEN=xoxb-...` (bot token) or `xoxp-...` (user token). Never hardcode or print tokens.
2. Grant the OAuth scopes listed in [references/api.md](references/api.md#scopes) (for example `chat:write`, `channels:read`, `channels:manage`, `files:write`, `users:read`).
3. Run scripts from any directory with `node <skill-dir>/scripts/<script>.cjs`. Append `--dry-run` to print the request without sending it.

## Operations

| Task | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Post a message | `node scripts/slack_post_message.cjs --channel "#general" --text "Hello <@U1234> :wave:"` |
| Schedule a message | `node scripts/slack_post_message.cjs --channel "#general" --text "Standup" --post-at 1710000000` |
| Reply in a thread | `node scripts/slack_post_message.cjs --channel C123 --text "Agreed" --thread-ts 1710000000.123456` |
| Post a Block Kit layout | `node scripts/slack_post_message.cjs --channel "#general" --blocks assets/blocks/announcement.json` |
| List channels | `node scripts/slack_list_channels.cjs` |
| Read channel history | `node scripts/slack_get_channel_history.cjs --channel C123 --limit 50` |
| Read a thread | `node scripts/slack_get_thread_replies.cjs --channel C123 --thread-ts 1710000000.123456` |
| Create a channel | `node scripts/slack_create_channel.cjs --name project-alpha` |
| Upload a file | `node scripts/slack_upload_file.cjs --file ./report.pdf --channels "#general" --initial-comment "Q3 report"` |
| Look up a user by email | `node scripts/slack_lookup_user.cjs --email ada@example.com` |

## Conventions

- Pass channels as `#name` or ID (`C...`); IDs are more reliable when the bot is not in the channel.
- `ts` values are float Unix timestamps; pass them as strings to `--thread-ts`, `--oldest`, and `--latest`.
- Scripts exit `2` on invalid arguments and `1` on API errors, printing a concise message (including the required scope when Slack reports a missing one).
- For rich layouts (headers, buttons, fields), see [references/blocks.md](references/blocks.md) and the templates in `assets/blocks/`.
- For endpoint details, pagination, rate limits, and scopes, see [references/api.md](references/api.md).

# Slack Web API Reference

Base URL: `https://slack.com/api/<method>`
Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. Never send the token in the request body.
All methods are POST with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` bodies, except `files.upload` which is `multipart/form-data`.
Responses are JSON with `ok: true` or `ok: false`. On failure, `error` holds a short code; `needed`/`provided` name missing scopes.

## Methods used by this skill

| Method | Purpose | Script |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `chat.postMessage` | Post a message | `slack_post_message.cjs` |
| `chat.scheduleMessage` | Schedule a message (`post_at`) | `slack_post_message.cjs` |
| `conversations.list` | List channels | `slack_list_channels.cjs` |
| `conversations.history` | Read channel history | `slack_get_channel_history.cjs` |
| `conversations.replies` | Read thread replies | `slack_get_thread_replies.cjs` |
| `conversations.create` | Create a channel | `slack_create_channel.cjs` |
| `files.upload` | Upload a file | `slack_upload_file.cjs` |
| `users.lookupByEmail` | Look up a user by email | `slack_lookup_user.cjs` |

## Scopes

| Scope | Needed for |
| --- | --- |
| `chat:write` | Post/schedule messages (bot tokens also need `chat:write.public` to post to public channels) |
| `channels:read` | List and read public channels |
| `groups:read`, `mpim:read`, `im:read` | Read private channels, group DMs, and DMs |
| `channels:manage` | Create, rename, and archive channels |
| `files:write` | Upload files |
| `users:read` | Look up users |

A missing-scope error returns `ok: false` with `needed: "..."`; the scripts print the required scope.

## Pagination

`conversations.list` and `conversations.history` return `response_metadata.next_cursor`. Pass that value as `cursor` to fetch the next page. `slack_list_channels.cjs` and `slack_get_channel_history.cjs` page automatically up to `--max` (default 1000 and 200 respectively) and print a hint with the cursor when more pages remain.

## Rate limits

Slack rate-limits each method by tier (roughly: Tier 3 ~50+ requests/min, Tier 2 ~20+/min, Tier 1 ~1/min). On a limit, the API returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header. Wait the suggested time and retry; for bulk jobs, sleep about 1 second between calls.

## Message formatting

Plain `text` supports Slack markdown:

- Bold `*text*`, italics `_text_`, code `` `code` ``, strikethrough `~text~`
- Mention a user `<@U1234>`, reference a channel `<#C123|name>`
- Link with a label `<https://example.com|Example>`
- Escape `&`, `<`, and `>` in literal text

For rich layouts (headers, buttons, fields, context lines, images), use Block Kit JSON via `--blocks` — see `blocks.md`.
